item.title: The Pit That Never Stopped: 450 Years of Mud, and the Men Who Tend It
item.description: Four fermentation pits in Luzhou have been working since 1573. The mud in their walls is the recipe nobody can copy, and the men who tend it cannot be replaced.

item.title: Baijiu 101: The Four Aromas, and Why Chinese Sort Liquor the Way They Sort Tea
item.description: Every baijiu bottle is stamped with one of four aroma types. What sauce, strong, light and rice actually mean, how the spirit ferments as solid grain, and how to drink your first glass.

item.title: The Moutai Puzzle: Why a Bottle Costs More Than Your Graphics Card
item.description: China's most famous spirit — sauce-aroma baijiu from Guizhou's Chishui River, worth more than Diageo.
